archetype.name: Bubble Team (goalie-split)
archetype.definition: A roughly even-strength team whose place in the standings swings on which goaltender plays and on finishing that has run well above the league's, sitting fifth in a crowded Central.

report.headline: Hofer and hot finishing carry a team that still gives up too much
report.take:
St. Louis is 13-9-2, 15th of 32 on the site, and fifth in a Central Division where only Chicago is clearly out of the race. On its season line this is a coin-flip team made slightly better. The Blues have 50.5% of the 5-on-5 expected goals (14th), only 49% of the shot attempts (21st), and a goal differential of +0.21 a game (14th). That is a real step up from last season's 37-33-12 club, which was 26th on the site, ran a -0.33 goal differential and won only 49.3% of the expected goals. But it is a middle-of-the-pack profile, not a contender's.

The record splits in two along the crease. Joel Hofer has started 17 games with a .919 save % and 9 goals saved above expected, fifth of 72 on the goalie tab. Jordan Binnington's seven starts produced a .847 save %, a -9.6 GSAx and a 4.77 GAA, 71st of 72. The two cancel almost exactly: the team's Goalies GSAx sits at 0.2, dead average. When Hofer plays, the Blues have a goaltending edge most nights. When Binnington plays, they are giving one away. The penalty kill matters as much as anything. It is at 83.1% (sixth), far above last year's 76.7%, and it is a big reason a team allowing 29.6 shots a game (29th) is only 17th in goals against.

The numbers hide two things. The first is finishing. The skaters are shooting 13.3% in all situations against a league average of 9.8%, and the all-situations PDO of 103 ranks sixth. The 5-on-5 PDO of 100.1 says even-strength luck is normal, so the hot shooting is concentrated elsewhere. Either way, 13.3% is the number most likely to fall. The second is the recent surge. The Blues are 4-1 over their last five, but they allowed 4.4 goals a game in that stretch while scoring 5.6: 8-6 over Anaheim, 9-6 over New Jersey, 5-4 in overtime against Edmonton. Wins like those come from outscoring a leak, not from fixing one.

The direction is still better than a year ago. October was a 7-7 grind and November is 6-4. The 96-point pace would be a ten-point jump on last season. I expect the shooting to cool and the pace to drift down toward the high 80s or low 90s. That puts the Blues squarely on the playoff bubble, with Hofer's workload as the biggest lever.

strengths.title: Hofer is a top-five goalie
strengths.body: Hofer has carried most of the starts with a .919 save % and 9 GSAx, numbers that rank him fifth on the goalie tab. Behind a team that allows plenty of shots, he is the main reason the Blues are not leaking goals. His save % is elite rather than absurd, so a strong level is plausible even if it eases a little.

strengths.title: Penalty kill transformed from last year
strengths.body: The PK is killing 83.1% of penalties, sixth in the league and well above the 77.2% average. Last season it was a below-average 76.7%. Part of that is Hofer, but the size of the jump and the team's suppression of opposing defensemen point to a structural fix. Opposing blueliners are held to the fewest points relative to expectation of any team. Some regression is likely, but a top-ten kill looks real.

strengths.title: Offense that can score in bunches
strengths.body: The Blues score 3.42 goals a game, 10th in the league and above the league's 3.2. Buchnevich leads the listed forwards with 11 points. Dvorsky has 6 goals on under 12 minutes a night with a 51.6% xGF share, a sign the depth is contributing. Some of the scoring is shooting luck, but the forwards grade a B, so a top-half offense is credible.

concerns.title: Too many shots against
concerns.body: The Blues allow 29.6 shots a game, 29th in the league and 2.6 above average. They lose the 5-on-5 attempt battle at 49%. The blueline grades only C+, and the defense ranks 17th in goals against even with Hofer and a top-six kill. That volume is the structural reason the record can swing hard on goaltending.

concerns.title: Binnington's starts are giving games away
concerns.body: Binnington's .847 save % and -9.6 GSAx rank 71st of 72. His seven starts erased everything Hofer saved, leaving the team's goaltending at league average. Unless Hofer can take nearly every start, the second goalie is the single biggest drag on the standings.

concerns.title: Finishing well above the league
concerns.body: The skaters are converting 13.3% of their shots against a 9.8% league average, and the all-situations PDO of 103 sits well above the league's 98.9. The last five games, at 5.6 goals scored and 4.4 allowed a game, are a team winning shootouts rather than controlling play. When the shooting cools, those 8-6 and 9-6 games turn into losses unless the goals against come down too.

trend.note: A 7-7 October gave way to a 6-4 November and a 4-1 last five, but goals against have climbed with the goals for, so the improvement is in results more than in control of games.

weekAhead.headline: Two elite goaltending teams, then a Washington side that leaks
weekAhead.body:
The week opens on the road against the Islanders, ninth on the site, with goalies at 13.4 GSAx (second) and an 85.1% penalty kill (fourth). Then comes Dallas, sixth on the site and 15-6-2, with A+ goaltending, the third-fewest shots allowed and an 88.8% kill. Both are the kind of opponent that cools a hot-shooting team: the Blues' finishing and middling power play run straight into goalies saving well above expected. The silver lining is offense. Dallas ranks 25th in goals and is shooting 4.9%, and the Islanders' power play is 29th, which suits the Blues' strong kill.

The week closes at home against Washington, 10-11-0 and 20th on the site. The Capitals control play well (53.5% xGF, sixth) but have F-grade goaltending, a .869 save % (30th) and the 30th-ranked defense. That is the game where St. Louis's finishing should play. With Dallas and Washington on consecutive days, how the Blues split the net may decide the week.

keyMatchups.title: Blues shooters vs Dallas goaltending
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows just 24.1 shots a game and its goalies have saved 12.7 goals above expected. A Blues attack shooting 13.3% will find far fewer easy goals. Dallas does give centers more than expected (24th), a possible opening down the middle.

keyMatchups.title: Blues PK vs Islanders power play
keyMatchups.body: The Islanders convert only 17.2% on the power play, 29th, against a Blues kill that ranks sixth. With Islanders goaltending near the top of the league, special teams are where St. Louis can avoid falling behind in a low-event game.

keyMatchups.title: Washington's leaky net
keyMatchups.body: Washington's goalies are at a .869 save % and -7.7 GSAx, and its defense ranks 30th. The Capitals out-chance opponents, so the Blues may give up volume again, but this is the best spot of the week to bank points.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts each game, above all on the Dallas–Washington back-to-back: Hofer's starts have been a different team from Binnington's.

restOfSeason.body:
The 96-point pace is built partly on shooting that sits well above the league and a recent run of high-scoring wins. Expect the finishing to cool and the scoring to drift from 3.42 a game toward the low 3s. The question is whether the goals against can come down to compensate. What should hold: Hofer's quality, a top-ten penalty kill, and 5-on-5 play that is roughly even and better than last year's. What should fade: the all-situations PDO of 103 and the 5-6 goal nights. I project 88 to 95 points and 39 to 43 wins. In this division that is a fight for a wild card rather than a comfortable spot.

The outlook moves most on the crease. If Hofer takes the large majority of the remaining 58 games and stays near his current level, the top of that range is realistic. If Binnington keeps starting regularly at his current form, the Blues slide toward the bottom of it. Cutting the shots against, now among the league's worst, is the only change that would make this team better than its bubble profile.

confidence.note: Only 24 games played; the goalie split and the finishing are big but unstable effects.
